newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures, alike, were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb lower, livestock analysts said.

Further pressure in live cattle futures was expected to stem from a weak tone to the fed cattle market. Futures declined to five-week lows Monday and should continue to trend lower as weakness expected in cash beef in the near term will likely keep packer bids for fed cattle lower, analysts said.

Weekend beef clearance at retail meat cases was hampered by wet and cool weather in some areas which curbed outdoor cooking and this will keep bids for cattle down as fed supplies are seen rising into the summer, they said.

Further gains expected in CBOT corn futures were again expected to weigh on feeder cattle futures along with spillover weakness from live cattle futures. Higher feed costs and declining profits should reduce demand for replacement feeders, analysts said.
Corn futures are seen trending higher this month and there is already a large supply of cattle on feed, sources noted.
The latest CME feeder cattle index rose $0.05 to $77.42 per cwt.
